Mountain glaciers store fresh water as compacted snow and ice, releasing it
gradually through summer melt. This seasonal release supports river flow
during dry months in many alpine regions.

Since the 1980s, most monitored mountain glaciers have lost mass overall,
though the rate of loss varies considerably by region and by decade. Glacier
mass balance is typically measured by comparing snow accumulation in winter
against ice and snow loss in summer.

Glacial retreat can reduce the reliability of downstream water supplies once
a glacier's ice reserves are depleted, because the buffering effect of stored
ice diminishes over time.
